analysis:
All changes are in the CI threat-review tooling under .github/scripts. They do not touch provider, native-runtime or coordinator code, so the retained provider threat entries (for example T-041) are not affected. I found no regression to a provider threat-model asset or boundary, and I report no qualifying finding.

Control-plane changes examined:
- threat-review-gate.py:34-35 now requires report['run'] to equal GITHUB_RUN_ID-attempt. budget_runner.py writes the same run_id into both the checkpoint and the result file, so this binds the clearance result to the current run and tightens stale-result reuse.
- budget_runner.py result delivery writes to a temp file and replaces atomically. An OSError raises ResultWriteFailure and the CLI exits 1 (threat-model-review.py:24-27, 34), so a failed write fails closed and cannot yield a clean result.
- budget_runner.py alive() now rejects closed or merged PRs and a changed revision, using ReviewFailure codes. This is stricter.
- bedrock.py:165-190 changes failed or missing usage accounting from raising an exception to setting accounting_stopped and still returning the response text. Later calls, fallback and repair are blocked through the stopped property and __call__ (lines 60, 86-92).

Open question for integration: the comment at bedrock.py:182-184 says stopped accounting blocks final merge clearance. That depends on the Scanner or runner (budget_scan.py, not supplied) checking paid.stopped, or the stop diagnostic, after the last call and recording an error or diagnostic. If the usage-record failure happens on the final call and nothing downstream checks stopped, the paid response could be accepted as a complete clean scan. That would mean spend was not accounted for and clearance is still granted. The base code failed closed by raising ReviewFailure. I could not verify this because budget_scan.py, state.py and the head side of budget_runner.py were not supplied, and the budget_runner.py head-side source was also not visible. It needs a check in the next pass.

The test-file changes only adapt tests to replay units using a source_id key. I could not review the replay_source implementation that produces it.
